title: Review of Monthly Household-income Ceiling for Prospective Buyers of BTO Flats and Executive Condominiums
what_it_is: Review of Monthly Household-income Ceiling for Prospective Buyers of BTO Flats and Executive Condominiums

sections.label: Income ceiling and housing grants
sections.summary: The income ceiling was last reviewed in 2019, when it was raised for new flats and ECs, and there are no plans to revise it now.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The income ceiling was last reviewed in 2019, when it was raised from $12,000 to $14,000 for families buying a new flat, and from $14,000 to $16,000 for families buying an EC from property developers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: At the same time, we introduced the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant, or the EHG, to better support lower- to middle-income families buying their first homes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: There are no plans to revise the income ceilings at this point.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: At the current income ceiling of $14,000, about eight in 10 Singaporeans are eligible to apply for a BTO flat, while the $16,000 ceiling enables about nine in 10 Singaporeans to apply for EC.

sections.label: Measures to cool resale market
sections.summary: Additional measures were rolled out in September 2022, including a 15-month wait-out period, and raising the income ceiling may negate efforts to cool the resale market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To this end, as the Member knows, we have rolled out additional measures in September 2022 to moderate demand and ensure prudent borrowing amidst rising interest rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And then to moderate demand for resale flats, MND and HDB introduced the 15-month wait-out period for private property owners and ex-private property owners to buy a non-subsidised HDB resale flat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Raising the income ceiling at this juncture may negate the efforts to cool the resale market as it would enable the higher-income households to bid up resale prices further.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Our other priority is to ramp up the supply of new flats to meet the strong demand for public housing.

sections.label: No plans to raise income ceiling
sections.summary: Housing grants and the income ceiling are separate matters, and there are no plans to increase the income ceiling at this stage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In so far as the grant is concerned, if the concern is whether or not their housing grant can be increased, that is something we can look at and make a separate decision because they are two separate things.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, if the Member is asking, today, can I say that we will increase the income ceiling, the answer is there are no plans to do that at this stage.
